claims.evidence: The witness confirmed it is an industrial machine, but the specific stitch type (straight stitch) requires seeing the needle plate or a sewing sample.

risks.risk: The electric motor may be burnt out or excessively noisy.
risks.proof: A video clip of the motor running and the machine sewing.

risks.risk: Mechanical timing may be off, causing skipped stitches or thread breakage.
risks.proof: A photo of a sewing sample produced by the machine.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a professional mechanical service

risks.risk: The internal oil pump may be failed or the reservoir empty, leading to seized parts.
risks.proof: A photo of the oil pan under the machine head showing oil level and clarity.
risks.if_unproven: as poorly maintained with potential internal wear

risks.risk: The drive belt may be frayed or snapped.
risks.proof: A photo of the belt connecting the motor to the handwheel.

proof_requests: Video of the machine powered on and sewing through at least two layers of fabric.
Photo of the underside of the machine head (oil pan area).
Clear photo of the needle plate and presser foot.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as an EMEL industrial sewing machine. It can be priced at its worst-case functional value given the visible cosmetic wear and unverified mechanical state.
